1.title: Off to the Vet!
1.topic: taking a pet dog with a hurt leg to the vet, who puts a pad on the cut (pets, community helpers, caring)
lines: We *get* in the *van*. | We *go* to the *vet*.
*Yes*, it is a *cut*. | She *puts* on a *red* *pad*. ↘
sounds: 입을 반쯤 벌리고 짧게 '에': leg '렉', vet '벳'. '에-이'처럼 늘이지 않아요.
입에 힘을 빼고 짧게 '어': cut '컷', hug '허그'.
v는 윗니로 아랫입술을 살짝 물고 '브으': van, vet. b는 두 입술을 붙였다 떼요: bad.
1.expression: Sound worried and slow on “His leg is bad.”, get moving on “We get in the van.”, lift your voice on the question “Is it a cut?”, sound gentle and calm while the vet helps, praise Gus warmly on “Good dog, Gus!” and finish happy and cozy on “I hug my dog.”

2.title: Taking Turns on the Swing
2.topic: a boy grabs the swing at recess, feels bad, says sorry and the two friends take turns pushing each other (school, friendship, feelings)
sounds: raced, reached, stomped, looked, walked, pushed
s, ch, p, k, sh 뒤의 -ed는 짧은 t: raced '레이스트', pushed '푸쉬트'.
b, l, n 같은 소리 뒤는 약한 d: grabbed '그랩드', smiled '스마일드'.
2.expression: Start fast and excited as Noah races to the swing, sound sharp and upset on “Hey! I was here first!”, make “stomped away” heavy and grumpy, slow down and sound quiet and lonely in the middle, say “I'm sorry I grabbed it” softly and honestly, let Ava's question go up kindly, and end bright and happy as they push each other.

3.title: Magnets: Push and Pull
3.topic: what magnets attract (iron and steel, not wood, plastic or paper), north and south poles that pull or push, and magnets in everyday life (science, how things work)
lines: Magnets *pull* on *things* made of *iron* or *steel*, | like *paper* *clips* and *nails*.
*Every* magnet has *two* *ends* | *called* *poles*: | a *north* pole and a *south* pole.
If you *put* a *north* pole *near* a *south* pole, | they *snap* *together*! ↘
sounds: invisible은 둘째 'VIS', together는 둘째 'GETH'에 힘! magnet, plastic은 첫 음절을 크게.
iron은 '아이언'처럼 읽어요. 'r' 소리를 따로 내지 않아요: '아이런' (X).
혀끝을 윗니 사이로 살짝 내밀고 바람: north '노r쓰', south '사우쓰'. 'ㅅ'나 'ㄷ'로 바꾸지 않아요.
3.expression: Read like a curious science presenter: sound amazed on “invisible power” and “without touching them!”, list iron, steel, paper clips and nails clearly, pause on each comma in “wood, plastic, or paper”, make “they snap together!” quick and surprising, make “push each other away” firm, and end with an inviting, friendly question.

4.title: The Lantern Walk
4.topic: a child makes a paper lantern for a neighborhood November lantern walk, feels nervous in the dark park, and learns from a neighbor that many small lights together light the path (community, seasons, feelings, courage)
lines: When the *nights* *grow* *long* in *November*, | the *families* on *Maple* *Street* | *hold* a *Lantern* *Walk*.
I *glued* *orange* and *yellow* *tissue* *paper* | onto an *old* *oatmeal* *box* | and *cut* *tiny* *stars* into the *sides*.
“*That's* *why* we *walk* *together*,” | she *said*. | “*Each* *lantern* is *small*, | but *together* we *light* the *whole* *path*.”
*Halfway* *around* the *pond*, | a *gust* of *wind* *tipped* my *candle* *over*, | and my *lantern* *went* *dark*. ↘
*Before* I could *panic*, | *Leo* *held* his *lantern* *close* to *mine*, | and *Dad* *set* my *candle* *upright* *again*.
When I *looked* *back*, | I *saw* a *long* *river* of *tiny* *lights* | *winding* through the *park*.
*Now* I *know* | the *dark* isn't *so* *scary* | when you *walk* it with *friends*. ↘
sounds: 대부분 첫 음절에 힘: LAN-tern '랜턴', NEIGH-bor '네이버'. together는 'GETH', upright는 'RIGHT'에 힘!
glued, whispered / placed, looked, tipped / started
모음·r 뒤는 약한 d(glued '글루드'), s·k·p 뒤는 짧은 t(placed '플레이스트'), t 뒤는 '이드'(started '스타r티드').
lined up, gust of wind, walk it with
자음+모음은 이어서: lined up '라인덥', gust of '거스터브', walk it '워킷'.
4.expression: Tell it like a quiet evening memory: cozy and proud while you make the lantern, slow and nervous as the sun goes down, make “spooky shadows” sound a little scary, whisper the worried question with your voice going up, give Mrs. Okafor a calm, warm voice, speed up a little when the lantern goes dark, sound amazed at the river of lights, and end slow and peaceful on the last line.
practice: a long river of tiny lights
